visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 consistently shows the correct ground-to-ground parabolic projectile setup and range relationship, while Lesson 2 includes sustained visual/math inaccuracies such as a horizontal launch depiction despite a 30° angle, an incorrect horizontal component labeled 40 cos 30 = 20 m/s, and a wrong flight-time display of 3.00 s.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 1 includes a functional, wired quiz gate after act_vertical_motion with a real question, options, and marked correct answer, whereas Lesson 2 has no gate specs or plan available, so it provides no verifiable interactivity.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 1 is clear, naturally paced, and uses well-spoken math terminology, while Lesson 2 contains multiple narration defects and garbled phrases such as “1 9.8 every second,” “0 verts,” “X2,” and an awkward repeated line.

sync.rationale: Lesson 1 provides mostly well-aligned visual cues that fire near the narrated references, while Lesson 2 has no beat or cue timing data at all, making synchronization impossible to verify and therefore materially weaker on this dimension.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 is more conceptually accurate and pedagogically clear because it explicitly derives vertical time from the height equation, explains independence of components, constant horizontal velocity, and the range formula, while Lesson 2 is mostly correct but much terser and includes confusing/garbled phrasing like “Gravity eats the upward speed, 1 9.8 every second” and “X2” that could hinder understanding.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 is far more polished with large, centered, visually consistent full-frame graphics, while Lesson 1 keeps a tiny nearly illegible diagram pushed into the upper-left with vast empty space, cramped top text, and distracting UI/overlay elements despite Lesson 2 having a few garbled labels.

aggregator.explanation: Five of six dimension agents strongly favor Lesson 1, all with high confidence: it is more visually accurate, interactive, better narrated, better synchronized, and more conceptually accurate. These include several substantive issues in Lesson 2, such as incorrect projectile visuals/math, missing interactivity specs, garbled narration, absent timing data, and confusing phrasing. Lesson 2 wins only on polish, also with high confidence, due to cleaner full-frame graphics and better visual presentation. However, that single advantage is outweighed by Lesson 1's broad and confident superiority across the core instructional and technical dimensions.
